raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my 20 mu.

---

My wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in October like everyone does here. Right now I'm watching it come out of dormancy. I used my usual variety, Jimai 22, saved some seed from last year and bought a bit to refresh. I put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting, so that's my base. That came to around 80 yuan per mu just for base fertilizer.

Now the extension station people came around last winter and said 15 kg N per mu is enough for wheat, but honestly I usually do a bit more — maybe 18 or 19 total. Last year I cut back once and the wheat looked yellow at jointing and I got nervous. Better to spend an extra 30 yuan than lose 50 kg of grain. So I'll topdress urea at jointing, about 20 kg of urea per mu (that's around 9 kg N).

Water — I'll irrigate the wheat 3 times this spring: return green in early March, jointing end of March, and grain filling in early May. Each irrigation costs me about 30 yuan per mu for the electricity and well time. If it rains well I might skip one, but I can't count on that. Last year my neighbor Old Wang skipped the grain-filling irrigation and his yield dropped maybe 50 kg/mu. I won't make that mistake.

Pesticides — I'll spray herbicide once in spring (the broadleaf weeds are getting bad) and watch for aphids and powdery mildew around heading. Usually need one insecticide spray in May.

For the maize, I plant right after wheat harvest — maybe June 13, soon as the combine is off the field. No time to plow, I do no-till direct seeding with the rented planter (30 yuan/mu for the custom operator). I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, about 4 kg/mu, costs me maybe 50 yuan/mu. I put down a compound fertilizer as base at planting, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage (around mid-July). Total maize N maybe 16-17 kg/mu. Extension says 14 is fine but again, I'd rather spend 20 extra yuan.

Maize needs less water here because summer rain comes. I might irrigate once at tasseling if July is dry. One irrigation in a normal year, zero if rain is good.

Family labor — my wife and I do most of it. My parents help at harvest. Two of the kids are in school, the older one works in Handan city and sends money home. We hire the combine for wheat harvest (50 yuan/mu) and maize harvest (60 yuan/mu), and the planter for both. Everything else we handle.

Total I'm spending maybe 750-800 yuan per mu across both crops for inputs, so around 15,000-16,000 yuan for the season. I keep some cash reserve — never put everything into inputs, in case the well pump breaks or someone gets sick.

Yield — I expect 450 kg/mu wheat and maybe 530 kg/mu maize in a normal year. That's what I got last year and the year before that was similar.
